name: Achaia
overview: The region of Achaia holds significant importance in the New Testament as a center of early Christian ministry and benevolence. Paul’s journeys included passing through Achaia with a clear purpose to strengthen the churches there, as seen in Acts 19:21 and 2 Corinthians 1:1. The believers in Achaia demonstrated notable generosity, contributing to the support of the poor saints in Jerusalem (Romans 15:26) and showing zeal in their ministry (1 Corinthians 16:15; 2 Corinthians 9:2). Additionally, the church in Achaia produced faithful followers like Epaenetus, recognized as the firstfruits unto Christ (Romans 16:5), underscoring the fruitfulness of the gospel in this region.
